university: The University of Texas at Austin

documents.unit: Office of the Executive Vice President and Provost, Office of Academic Technology
documents.title: AI for Teaching & Learning Toolkit: Policy & Recommendations
tiers: permitted / prohibited / partially permitted (instructor chooses per course)
documents.summary: The Provost's Office of Academic Technology toolkit page requires every syllabus to carry a course AI policy and leaves the choice of permitted, prohibited or partially permitted to each course. It adds disclosure recommendations, allows instructors to require AI where essential, does not endorse detectors, asks for human review of AI used in grading, and links to other offices.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no single university stance: it says 'Every syllabus must include a course AI policy that designates whether AI is permitted, prohibited, or partially permitted', handing the decision to instructors, so the stance is delegates.

units.why: The page opens by saying the university 'has issued guidance on many aspects of generative AI', framing the toolkit as an institution-level framework; I chose P56 (framework/scope) because it states purpose and scope, not a rule.
units.anchor: has issued guidance on many aspects of generative AI and other AI technologies on campus

units.why: The Resolving Academic Misconduct link describes 'reporting an incident of academic misconduct like unauthorized use of AI', which classes unauthorized AI use as misconduct handled through Student Affairs, so P36 (P81 not chosen: no procedural steps given).
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P36, informs, when-misuse. They differed on actor (A instructor, B all) and on the policy wording. The passage is a link in a teaching toolkit for the person who reports an incident, i.e. the instructor, so actor is instructor. B's wording ('incident of academic misconduct, reported through the Division of Student Affairs process') follows the source more closely than A's 'handled through', so B's policy is kept.
units.anchor: academic misconduct like unauthorized use of AI
units.policy: Unauthorized use of AI is an incident of academic misconduct, reported through the Division of Student Affairs process.

units.why: The library entry says it gives guidance on 'disclosing AI use, avoiding plagiarism and hallucinated sources, and citing generative AI', a pointer to disclosure and citation guidance; P24 fits best although it is only a pointer and also touches verification (P31).
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. The source says University Libraries provides 'guidance for students and instructors on disclosing AI use, avoiding plagiarism and hallucinated sources, and citing generative AI'. It is a real, if pointer-style, statement about disclosure guidance, so it is kept as P24 with A's fit note.
units.anchor: disclosing AI use, avoiding plagiarism and
units.policy: University Libraries provides guidance for students and instructors on disclosing AI use, avoiding plagiarism and hallucinated sources, and citing generative AI in APA, MLA and Chicago style.
units.fit_note: A pointer to guidance; also mentions avoiding hallucinated sources (P31) and citation styles (P25).

units.why: The Acceptable Use entry directs readers to 'uses of AI that are allowable and prohibited under University guidance and state law', a pointer on data and tool rules; P77 (comply with law and university policy) fits.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P77, should, general, all. A wrote a normalized policy, B left it null. The anchor alone ('allowable and prohibited under University guidance and state law') does not say who should do what, so A's normalized wording is kept; it adds nothing beyond 'Become familiar with uses of AI that are allowable and prohibited'.
units.anchor: allowable and prohibited under University guidance and state law
units.policy: Users should become familiar with the uses of AI that are allowable and prohibited under University guidance and state law.

units.why: The Decision Matrix entry tells readers to 'understand what kinds of data can be used with which tools', a data-protection and vetted-tool pointer, so P50.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P50 and should. A set phase general, B during-work. The Decision Matrix entry is a pointer to knowing which data may go with which tools, not tied to a stage of student work, so general. A's normalized wording is kept because the bare anchor lacks the 'understand' duty.
units.anchor: what kinds of data can be used with which tools
units.policy: Users should understand what kinds of data can be used with which tools (Local and Cloud Services Decision Matrix).

units.why: The graduate-education entry offers 'recommendations for departments creating and maintaining generative AI policies for graduate students', so departments are expected to write their own policies; P85 (units set own rules) fits, not P04 because it addresses departments.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P85, admin, before-course. Modality differed (A informs, B should). The source line is a link description ('Explore a set of recommendations for departments creating and maintaining generative AI policies for graduate students'): it describes a resource and does not tell departments what to do, so informs. B's fit note is kept, merged.
units.anchor: recommendations for departments creating and maintaining generative AI policies for graduate students
units.fit_note: Offers recommendations to departments rather than stating they may set their own rules; also mentions maintaining policies and research use.

units.why: "UT Austin provides free access to a variety of AI tools" is an institution-wide provision of tools at no cost, which P92 (university-provided tools, not one course) covers. P17 does not fit because it is not course-specific.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. The FAQ says 'UT Austin provides free access to a variety of AI tools', an institution-wide provision of tools. It is a real statement. P92 (institution-wide, not one course) is kept over P17, which is course-specific. A coded only the Sage sentence of the same passage, as P17. Unit stance encourage is kept from B because the provision invites use.
units.anchor: UT Austin provides free access to a variety of
units.policy: UT Austin provides free access to a variety of AI tools.

units.why: "UT Sage lets you design custom tutors that can be accessed by students in Canvas" describes a university-provided platform for course-specific tutor bots, the P17 example.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P17, instructor, before-course, encourage. Modality differed (A informs, B may). The source states what the tool does ('UT Sage lets you design custom tutors that can be accessed by students in Canvas'); it grants no permission, so informs. B's anchor is kept.
units.anchor: UT Sage lets you design custom tutors that can be accessed by students in Canvas

units.why: The FAQ says 'UT does not endorse AI-detection software and holds no central contract for it', so the university gives instructors no sanctioned detector; closest type is P39 (do not rely on detectors), though it states non-endorsement rather than unreliability.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P39, informs, when-misuse. They differed on actor (A instructor, B all) and unit_stance (A restrict, B neutral). The FAQ question is 'Which AI detector tool can I use with student work?' so the reader is the instructor. The answer 'UT does not endorse AI-detection software and holds no central contract for it' states a fact and forbids nothing, so neutral, not restrict. Fit notes of A and B are merged.
units.anchor: UT does not endorse AI-detection software and holds no central contract for it.
units.fit_note: States non-endorsement and no central contract, not that detectors are unreliable or cannot be used as proof.

units.why: 'Every syllabus must include a course AI policy' is a mandatory syllabus statement binding instructors in all courses, so P09, must, before-course. The what-it-must-designate part is coded as a separate unit.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P09, instructor, before-course, must. A split the sentence into two units (the syllabus requirement, and the permitted/prohibited/partially-permitted designation); B kept one unit. The source sentence states two distinct rules, so A's split is followed and this unit carries only the first rule with a null policy (the anchor states it).
units.anchor: Every syllabus must include a course AI policy

units.why: The same sentence requires the policy to 'designate whether AI is permitted, prohibited, or partially permitted', leaving the choice to each course; I chose P04 (each instructor sets the rule) over P05 because the three categories are what the instructor selects, not a defined tier scheme with named levels.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this second rule in the same sentence; B merged it into the P09 unit. The source requires the policy to designate 'whether AI is permitted, prohibited, or partially permitted, with clear conditions for use', which leaves the choice to each course. That is a distinct rule from having a syllabus statement, so it is kept as P04 with A's fit note.
units.anchor: designates whether AI is permitted, prohibited, or partially permitted, with clear conditions for use
units.policy: Each course's AI policy designates whether AI is permitted, prohibited, or partially permitted, with clear conditions for use.
units.fit_note: Also names three categories of use (P05) without defining tiers.

units.why: "give written instructions on what is allowed and how students should disclose their use" tells instructors who permit AI what to put in writing. It is about communicating expectations, so P09 rather than P24 (which binds students to disclose).
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P09, instructor, course-start, must, permit. They differed only in wording (A null, B normalized) and anchor span. B's normalized statement is kept because the condition 'If you permit or partially permit AI' is not in the anchor. A's fit note (P24 also touched) is kept; B's reason for P09 over P24 matches A's.
units.anchor: give written instructions on what is allowed and how students should disclose their use
units.policy: Instructors who permit or partially permit AI give written instructions on what is allowed and how students should disclose their use.
units.fit_note: Also requires telling students how to disclose AI use (P24).

units.why: The sentence points instructors to 'sample statements in Your Syllabus at UT Austin', offering templates for the required syllabus policy; P09 (syllabus statement) fits.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. The source says 'See the sample statements in Your Syllabus at UT Austin', offering templates for the required syllabus policy. It is a short pointer tied to the syllabus requirement, so it is kept as P09.
units.anchor: See the sample statements in
units.policy: Sample AI syllabus statements are provided in Your Syllabus at UT Austin.

units.why: Instructors may require generative AI "if such use is essential to the assessment of course learning outcomes". This permits requiring AI under a condition, so P79 (require AI in coursework), modality may, stance require.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave identical codes (P79, may, before-course, require); only topics differed. B's topics are kept, since the source ties requiring AI to 'assessment of course learning outcomes'.
units.anchor: Yes, if such use is essential to the assessment of course learning outcomes.

units.why: "we suggest that instructors provide accommodations to students with reasonable objections" is an equity/alternative-access rule for recommended-but-not-required AI tools, P51, with should.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P51, instructor, before-course, should. A kept policy null, B normalized it. The anchor omits the condition 'Where the tools are recommended but not required', so B's normalized policy is kept; 'we suggest' maps to should.
units.anchor: we suggest that instructors provide accommodations to students with reasonable objections
units.policy: Where AI tools are recommended but not required, instructors should provide accommodations to students with reasonable objections.

units.why: 'In all cases, use of AI tools should be carried out responsibly' is a general expectation on AI use in the classroom, closest to P56 as a general principle with no specific content.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. The source says 'In all cases, use of AI tools should be carried out responsibly'. It is a general principle, closest to P56, and kept with A's fit note that it has no specific content.
units.anchor: use of AI tools should be carried out responsibly
units.fit_note: Very general principle; no specific content on what responsible use means.

units.why: "Diligence about transparent use is a key aspect of AI fluency" gives the reason for disclosure by tying it to AI fluency as a skill. Nearest type is P44 (AI use as a professional skill), though the passage is about transparency, hence a fit note.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P44, all, general, informs. B added a fit note (it frames transparent disclosure itself as part of AI fluency); A's topics are in a different order. B's fit note is kept; no disagreement on codes.
units.anchor: Diligence about transparent use is a key aspect of AI fluency.
units.fit_note: Frames transparent disclosure itself as part of AI fluency; it does not claim employers expect AI skills.

units.why: The Office 'recommends that appropriate citations and AI disclosure statements be included in significant work products', a recommendation (not a mandate) to disclose AI use with submissions; P24 with should.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P24, student, during-work, should, permit. They differed on wording: B's normalized policy drops the word 'recommends', turning a recommendation into a plain statement. A's null policy with the anchor 'recommends that appropriate citations and AI disclosure statements be included in significant work products' states the rule exactly, so null is kept.
units.anchor: recommends that appropriate citations and AI disclosure statements be included in significant work products

units.why: 'Check your discipline's or professional organization's style guide' defers the format of AI disclosure to disciplinary style guides; P24 is nearest, but this is about format, not tool or prompt detail (P25).
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P24, all, during-work, should, neutral with the same fit note. B's anchor was copied from a different sentence ('many reasons to think twice...'), so A's anchor, which matches the source, is kept.
units.anchor: how to appropriately disclose AI use in your context.
units.policy: Check your discipline's or professional organization's style guide for how to appropriately disclose AI use.
units.fit_note: Defers disclosure format to the discipline's style guide; does not say what details to include.

units.why: On AI grading the FAQ says 'many reasons to think twice before automating aspects of the teaching and feedback process', discouraging but not forbidding instructor AI use in feedback; P59 (instructor use of AI) fits, with P101 used for the conditions below.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P59, instructor, during-work, should-not, restrict. B added a fit note; it is merged with A's. The source ('many reasons to think twice before automating aspects of the teaching and feedback process') cautions, so should-not and restrict stand.
units.anchor: many reasons to think twice before automating aspects of the teaching and feedback process
units.fit_note: Cautions rather than forbids or permits automating teaching and feedback; the P46 human-grades rule is not stated.

units.why: 'Instructor guidance is a crucial part of the learning process' gives the reason for caution about automating feedback; it is rationale about human instruction by instructors, which no rationale type captures, so UNCOVERED.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. The source says 'Instructor guidance is a crucial part of the learning process', the stated reason for caution about automating feedback. It is rationale; no type covers rationale about instructor feedback (P41 is about student practice), so UNCOVERED is kept with A's note.
units.anchor: Instructor guidance is a crucial part of the learning process.
units.uncovered_note: Rationale that instructor guidance and feedback are essential to learning, offered as a reason not to automate feedback.

units.why: The toolkit quotes Texas law: AI "must not autonomously make or be a controlling factor in making consequential decisions without meaningful human review", naming grading and evaluation of academic work. This is about decisions about people, so P73; P46 is the narrower grading-only rule and this covers more (curriculum, research).
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P73, all, general, must-not, restrict. B's anchor was copied from the next sentence (human-in-the-loop), so A's anchor is used. A left policy null but its anchor does not include the grading, curriculum and research list, so B's normalized policy, which follows the source ('under Texas law, AI tools must not...'), is kept. A's fit note is kept.
units.anchor: make or be a controlling factor in making consequential decisions without meaningful human review
units.policy: AI tools must not autonomously make or be a controlling factor in making consequential decisions without meaningful human review; the decisions include grading, the evaluation of academic work, the development of curriculum and teaching materials, and the conducting of research.
units.fit_note: The listed decisions include grading, evaluation of academic work, curriculum and teaching materials, and research (P46, P59, P62); P73 is chosen because the rule covers consequential decisions generally.

units.why: "you should exercise the practice of human-in-the-loop... making sure that you review all output since you are solely responsible" sets conditions for instructors using AI in teaching or grading (human review, sole responsibility), so P101.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P101, instructor, during-work, should, permit. They differed on wording and anchor. The source says 'you should exercise the practice of human-in-the-loop when you do use AI tools, making sure that you review all output since you are solely responsible for the result', so a normalized policy is needed to carry both parts; B's is kept with 'should' explicit. A's anchor is kept as the more load-bearing span.
units.anchor: making sure that you review all output since you are solely responsible for the result
units.policy: Instructors who use AI tools should exercise the practice of human-in-the-loop, review all output, and are solely responsible for the result.

units.why: 'grading systematically with machine learning might be acceptable for some assignments' permits some automated grading, while the next clause warns generative AI is not reliably consistent; P101 (conditions for AI grading) fits.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P101, instructor, during-work. A coded may/restrict, B informs/neutral. B's anchor was copied from another sentence. The source says 'While grading systematically with machine learning might be acceptable for some assignments, generative AI tools do not, by design, consistently and reliably produce the same output every time': a caution with a reason that neither grants a permission nor sets a ban, so informs and neutral. A's anchor and faithful normalized policy are kept; B's fit note is merged.
units.anchor: grading systematically with machine learning might be acceptable for some assignments
units.policy: Grading systematically with machine learning might be acceptable for some assignments, but generative AI tools do not, by design, consistently and reliably produce the same output every time.
units.fit_note: States that systematic machine-learning grading may be acceptable and why generative AI is unreliable for grading; no explicit condition on use.

units.why: Instructors unsure what kind of AI an academic technology tool uses are told to 'reach out to the Office of Academic Technology', which is faculty support for understanding AI; P63 fits.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P63 and instructor. A coded before-course, should, neutral; B general, may, encourage. The source is an offer of help ('please reach out to the Office of Academic Technology'), not a duty, so may; it is not tied to a course stage, so general; it says nothing about AI use itself, so neutral rather than encourage. B's anchor was copied from another sentence, so A's is used.
units.anchor: reach out to the Office of Academic Technology

documents.title: Acceptable Use of Generative AI Tools
documents.summary: The Information Security Office sets data and tool rules for generative AI across the university: what data may go into which tools, which tools are unapproved, and the Texas-law limit on AI making consequential decisions. It says little about coursework itself.
documents.stance_why: The page allows AI use with conditions ('may be used freely' for public data; Controlled data only with university-contracted tools) and prohibits unauthorized tools and fraudulent use, so it permits AI under conditions rather than banning or delegating.

units.why: The preamble says the guidance outlines 'acceptable practices for utilizing generative AI tools while safeguarding institutional, personal, and proprietary information', stating purpose and scope; P56 fits.
units.anchor: outlines acceptable practices for utilizing generative AI tools while safeguarding institutional, personal, and proprietary information

units.why: The preamble describes the covered tools as 'large language models (LLM), diffusion models, or generative AI applications', defining what the guidance covers; P61.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. The source defines the covered tools ('ChatGPT, Copilot, Bard Gemini, Claude and other generative AI applications known as large language models (LLM), diffusion models'), which sets what the guidance covers. It is a real definition, so it is kept as P61.
units.anchor: generative AI applications known as large language models (LLM), diffusion models, or generative AI applications

units.why: 'developed collaboratively by the Office of Legal Affairs, University Compliance Services, the Information Security Office, and the Business Contracts Office' states who made the guidance; P84.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P84, admin, informs. Phase differed (A before-course, B general). The sentence states who developed the guidance, a fact about the document rather than a stage of course work, so general.
units.anchor: developed collaboratively by the Office of Legal Affairs, University Compliance Services, the Information Security Office

units.why: "Additional guidance may be forthcoming as circumstances evolve" says the guidance is provisional, P54.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P54, informs, over-time. Actor differed (A all, B admin). The statement is the issuing offices saying they may add guidance, so admin.
units.anchor: Additional guidance may be forthcoming as circumstances evolve.

units.why: Public or Published data 'may be used freely with AI tools' is a permission tied to data classification; closest type is P50 (protect data, vetted tools) as the permissive side of the same data-classification rule.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P50, all, may, permit. Phase differed (A general, B during-work). The rule classifies data and is not tied to a stage of student work, so general. The two fit notes say the same and are merged.
units.anchor: may be used freely with AI tools
units.policy: Data that is publicly available or classified as Published university information may be used freely with AI tools.
units.fit_note: A permission for public data rather than a protection; it is the permissive end of the data-classification rule.

units.why: Controlled or Confidential data 'can be used with AI tools that are managed by the university and covered by contracts explicitly protecting university data', limiting sensitive data to vetted tools; P50.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P50, all, may, restrict. Phase differed (A general, B during-work); it is a data-classification rule, so general. A's anchor is kept, since it is the exact span.
units.anchor: can be used with AI tools that are managed by the university and covered

units.why: The contracts must ensure data is not used for training or is isolated, and 'web search functionality must be disabled', a specific technical condition on vetted tools; P50 is nearest but the web-search rule is more specific.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P50, all, must, restrict. Phase differed (A general, B during-work); a data-classification rule, so general. A's and B's fit notes agree and are merged.
units.anchor: web search functionality must be disabled
units.fit_note: Adds contract conditions (no training, isolated instance) and a requirement to disable web search; a concrete technical condition on contracted tools.

units.why: The Local and Cloud Services Decision Matrix 'provides information on AI tools and the types of university data authorized for use with each tool', i.e. the approved-tool list; P92.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P92, all, general, informs. No disagreement on codes; B's extra topic is kept.
units.anchor: provides information on AI tools and the types of university data authorized

units.why: 'use should be consistent with the Acceptable Use Policy' ties AI use to an existing university policy, P77.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P77, all, general, should. A normalized the policy, B left it null; the source reads 'In all cases, use should be consistent with the Acceptable Use Policy', and A's wording adds the subject (AI use) that the anchor lacks, so A's is kept.
units.anchor: use should be consistent with the
units.policy: In all cases, AI use should be consistent with the Acceptable Use Policy.

units.why: Tools without a contract "are not approved for use with Controlled or Confidential university information", a prohibition tied to vetting, P50 (P92 is the positive duty to use approved tools).
units.resolution_why: A coded P92 (use approved tools), B coded P50. The source says tools that lack a university contract 'are not approved for use with Controlled or Confidential university information': it protects confidential data by limiting it to vetted tools, which is P50's 'protect personal and confidential data; prefer vetted tools'. P92 is the duty to use approved tools generally, institution-wide. P50 is kept; A's fit note is merged.
units.anchor: AI tools that lack a university contract and appropriate data-sharing controls are not approved
units.fit_note: Frames the rule as what is not approved for Controlled or Confidential data rather than as a duty to use approved tools (P92).

units.why: The list names 'AI Detection software' among tools not approved for Controlled or Confidential data, so detector use with student information is restricted; no type covers a detector-specific data rule, so P50 with a fit note.
units.resolution_why: A coded P50 with actor instructor; B coded P39 with actor all. The source lists 'AI Detection software' among the tools that lack a contract and are not approved for Controlled or Confidential data. The rule is about protecting data, which is P50; P39 is about detector reliability or not relying on detectors, which the passage does not say. The rule binds all users, so actor all. A normalized policy is added because the anchor alone does not state the rule. Fit notes are merged.
units.anchor: free or non-UT-managed versions of AI tools like ChatGPT and Copilot, and AI Detection software
units.policy: AI Detection software, like other AI tools that lack a university contract and appropriate data-sharing controls, is not approved for use with Controlled or Confidential university information.
units.fit_note: Specifically places AI detection software among unapproved tools for sensitive data, which also bears on detection (P39/P40); it does not say detectors are unreliable.

units.why: 'Student records subject to FERPA, health information, proprietary information' must not be used with unauthorized AI tools, a must-not data-protection rule; P50.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P50, all, must-not, prohibit. Phase differed (A general, B during-work); the rule bans putting sensitive records into unauthorized tools and is not tied to a stage of student work, so general.
units.anchor: must not be used with unauthorized AI tools

units.why: Texas law 'prohibits state agencies, including UT Austin, from deploying AI intended to autonomously make or be a controlling factor in making consequential decisions without meaningful human review', listing grading, admissions, discipline and academic integrity; P73.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P73, admin, general, must-not. Unit stance differed (A prohibit, B restrict). The law bars deployment only 'without meaningful human review', so AI is allowed with human review: restrict. A normalized policy is added because the anchor stops mid-sentence.
units.anchor: prohibits state agencies, including UT Austin, from deploying AI intended to autonomously make
units.policy: Texas state law prohibits state agencies, including UT Austin, from deploying AI intended to autonomously make or be a controlling factor in making consequential decisions without meaningful human review.
units.fit_note: The list of consequential decisions includes grading, student conduct and academic integrity, admissions, hiring, and research evaluation.

units.why: 'UT Austin's CISO must review AI tools to be used for any of these purposes prior to their procurement, development, deployment, or use' requires approval before deployment; P65.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P65, admin, before-course, must. Unit stance differed (A restrict, B neutral). The review is a gate that must pass before the tools are used for these decisions, so restrict. The policy is normalized because 'any of these purposes' in the anchor refers to the preceding list.
units.anchor: CISO must review AI tools to be used for any of these purposes
units.policy: UT Austin's CISO must review AI tools to be used for any of the listed consequential decisions prior to their procurement, development, deployment, or use.

units.why: "AI tools must not be used for activities that are illegal, fraudulent, or violate any state or federal laws, or UT Austin or UT System policies" is a general conduct ban; P74 (fraud) chosen over P77 because the heading and core concern is illegal and fraudulent activity.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P74, all, general, must-not, prohibit. A left policy null with a short anchor, B normalized it. The anchor stops before 'or violate any state or federal laws, or UT Austin or UT System policies', so B's full statement is kept, with its fit note (P77 territory). Both chose P74 over P77 because the heading is 'Fraudulent or Illegal Activities'.
units.anchor: AI tools must not be used for activities that are illegal, fraudulent
units.policy: AI tools must not be used for activities that are illegal, fraudulent, or violate any state or federal laws, or UT Austin or UT System policies.
units.fit_note: Also bans violating laws and university policies (P77 territory).

units.why: Click-through agreements "may result in personal responsibility for compliance with the terms and conditions of the AI tool", a warning about tool terms of use, nearest P52.
units.resolution_why: A coded UNCOVERED with modality should; B coded P52 with informs. P52 covers 'terms of use', and the passage is about the terms and conditions of the AI tool, so P52 is the nearest type, but it is about personal liability, not licensing or ownership. The passage says 'Be aware that...may result in', a warning of fact, so informs. Phase is general (B had during-work). A's uncovered concern is kept in the fit note.
units.anchor: accepting click-through agreements without delegated signature authority may result in personal responsibility
units.frag_end: terms and conditions of the AI tool.
units.policy: Accepting click-through agreements without delegated signature authority may result in personal responsibility for compliance with the terms and conditions of the AI tool.
units.fit_note: About personal liability for accepting a tool's terms of use rather than copyright or ownership of outputs. Coder A judged that no type covers it (a warning that accepting click-through terms without signature authority can make the individual personally responsible).

units.why: "ensure compliance with IRUSP Standard 22" for AI tools from external vendors is a vendor and third-party review requirement, P65.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P65, all, must. Phase differed (A general, B before-course) and unit stance (A restrict, B neutral). The requirement 'ensure compliance with IRUSP Standard 22' applies whenever external-vendor tools are engaged, not at a course stage, so general. It sets a compliance condition without limiting or encouraging use, so neutral.
units.anchor: ensure compliance with IRUSP Standard 22

units.why: The page points to the 'UT.AI Hub for solutions, training, and community conversations', offering training and resources; P70.
units.resolution_why: Both chose P70, all, general, encourage. Modality differed (A should, B may). The source is the imperative 'Explore the UT.AI Hub for solutions, training, and community conversations', a recommendation rather than a bare permission, so should.
units.anchor: Explore the UT.AI Hub for solutions, training, and community conversations

units.why: Users with appropriate-use questions are told to 'contact the UT Information Security Office', which names the office to ask; P80 is nearest but this is a contact point, not interpretation or enforcement authority.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. The source says 'For questions regarding the appropriate use of ChatGPT and other AI Tools, please contact the UT Information Security Office'. It names the office to ask. It is a thin statement, but it does name who answers questions on appropriate use, so it is kept as P80 with A's fit note.
units.anchor: please contact the UT Information Security Office at
units.fit_note: A contact for questions rather than a statement that the office interprets or enforces the policy.

units.why: The revision history shows 'Added Heightened Scrutiny AI to the prohibited use list to align with Texas state law', evidence that the policy is revised over time; P54.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this. The revision-history entry 'Added Heightened Scrutiny AI to the prohibited use list to align with Texas state law' is evidence that the guidance is revised over time. B skipped the revision history as repeats. It is not a repeat of the Heightened Scrutiny rule: it records a revision and its reason, so it is kept as P54. Other history entries are not coded.
